key_insight: There is no single best generative model for producing a diverse set of valid answers; learning a lightweight router that selects which model or sampling strategy to use per prompt yields higher "diversity coverage" than relying on any single model.
problem_solved: Generative systems often miss many valid responses for prompts that admit many correct answers; existing evaluation and sampling methods don't prioritize covering unique, high-quality answers across outputs.
method: Define a new metric, diversity coverage, which measures total quality across unique answers relative to the optimal set of the same size.
Train a router that, given an input prompt, selects among multiple models or sampling configurations to maximize the diversity coverage of the produced answer set.
Combine outputs from heterogeneous models via the router and evaluate against baselines (single-model sampling, uniform mixtures) to show improved coverage.
impact: Provides a practical way to generate more comprehensive, non-redundant answer sets for open-ended prompts, improving user satisfaction, dataset creation, and downstream evaluation. Enables practitioners to leverage model ensembles more effectively for diversity-sensitive tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt -> learned router -> pool of models/sampling strategies -> diverse unique answers (annotated with quality scores)
Bar chart comparing diversity coverage across: single model, uniform mixture, and learned router (showing router leads)
Coverage curve: number of unique high-quality answers vs. number of samples per method
Example prompt box with side-by-side diverse outputs from different routed models to illustrate qualitative difference
paper_title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
